summary: The base reproducibly lets LMCache and FlexKV exceed kv_len_to_handle. The exact candidate caps both normal and speculative backend-derived lengths before token and KV-index slicing, and passed its regression plus independent boundary cases.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: both backends stored 9 rather than 4 entries normally and 8 rather than 4 speculatively; 4 failed and 2 passed backend subtests.
Candidate regression: 3 tests passed and 6 backend subtests passed.
Sixteen independent LMCache/FlexKV cases across topk None/1/2/8 and smaller/equal/larger caller bounds; all token and KV-index lengths matched min(backend-derived length, caller limit).

gpu_execution.evidence: ROCm and torch identify the assigned device as AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950/capability (9,5), but tests exercised CPU-side metadata slicing only.

remaining_limitations: LMCache and FlexKV packages/services were unavailable; optional dependencies were stubbed while actual SGLang backend methods were executed.
No live asynchronous external-store integration was run.
The prepared ROCm gfx950 environment differs from the issue's NVIDIA CUDA environment.
No model, semantic-accuracy, distributed, or multi-node claim is made.
No native code changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
